analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/hardware-support.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one documentation paragraph (head lines 56-70) on pipeline decode command-buffer memory pricing. It contains no code, configuration, key handling, attestation or transport changes. I examined the base excerpt (lines 878-1255, unchanged context) and the head excerpt (lines 1-449). The paragraph says each request charge for Qwen, Nemotron, Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS prices every attending layer's decode rows together, with a floor of one prompt frame's attention transient. It states that LOAD quotes and activation floors are unchanged, and that only requests with prompt frames shorter than their decode rows are charged more. This makes admission more conservative, which is a memory-availability matter (TB-007, T-029/T-016 adjacent) and not a weakening of any control. I found no effect on A-001 prompt confidentiality, attestation (TB-009, TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), the fan helper, or the add-on hold socket. The excerpt also notes that attention-kernel partials beyond the priced rows are not charged, and it does not claim a memory-safety guarantee, so it does not overclaim. The paragraph references the anchor inference.md#pipeline-decode-command-buffers and the symbols QwenResidentPrefillTransient, Gemma4PrefillTransient and GPTOSSRequestStateBudget. I could not verify that these exist, because the source files and the inference.md target were not supplied. That is a documentation-accuracy question and not a security regression. No threat-model update is needed from this change.
